name: Invoice document (header band + lines table + totals)
description: The classic transactional document: a bold label/value header band (customer, number, date, terms), a bordered line-items table, and a shaded totals row summing the lines. Batch runs put one document per page. Fits invoices, credit memos, packing lists, order confirmations.
whenToUse: The ask is a printable document per business transaction with identity fields on top and its lines below. TWO levels only (document > lines) - a third level (customer > invoice > lines) is lp:archetype:statement-run instead. Print/PDF/Word delivery -> RTF.
intents: invoice layout with customer details on top and line items below
packing list with header fields and a lines table
credit memo with a totals row under the item table
printable document per order showing its lines and total
invoice header band then items then amount due

requires.dataShape: one G_INVOICE node per document carrying the header fields, with nested G_LINE rows (datamodel groupBy); ORDER BY invoice then line in the SQL
requires.preAggregation: any header-band total (amount due, tax) as a SQL column on G_INVOICE; the lines sum in the totals row is template-side sum(G_LINE/FIELD)

composition.notes: splitByPage:true on the outer forEach = one page per invoice; add page.header/footer blocks for running furniture; subtemplate chrome composes like lp:archetype:form-letter

pitfalls: The lines table forEach is RELATIVE (G_LINE) under the outer forEach - an absolute inner path repeats every line of every invoice under each invoice and totals go global (see lp:anti:absolute-inner-group).
Totals cells are {col, expr|label, span}; the sum path is relative to the invoice context: sum(G_LINE/LINE_AMOUNT).
Bind placeholder names (G_INVOICE, LINE_AMOUNT) to YOUR datamodel output tree before building.

Side-by-side chart|table placement -> switch the stack to the grid form (lp:technique:xpt-grid-chart-table); print-first fixed geometry -> lp:archetype:print-dashboard.
intents: monitoring dashboard with kpis charts and detail tables
operations dashboard: headline numbers then status pie then last 24h table
one dashboard page with a chart and several filtered views of the data

requires.dataShape: one detail-grain group (e.g. G_ROW: REQUEST_ID, STATUS, RUN_DAY, DAYS_AGO) feeds the charts AND the filtered tables; plus a single-row KPI group (G_KPI) whose headline totals are SQL columns
requires.preAggregation: KPI values via SQL aggregates in a one-row dataset/group; charts aggregate the detail rows themselves (count/sum) - do NOT pre-pivot into wide columns

composition.notes: flat stack order is fixed: kpis, then charts, then tables; a grid replaces the stack when side-by-side is wanted; every chart is wired for click-to-filter automatically

Filter tables with filters:[{field,operator,value}], never an XPath predicate (see lp:anti:xpath-predicate-on-xpt-datatable); a chart's aggregation MAY use the XPath filter knob.
Headline numbers are kpis cards, not a one-row table (see lp:anti:headline-kpis-as-table).

name: Print dashboard (RTF grid: chart | chart + full-width table)

email a one page report with charts on top

requires.preAggregation: none needed for the charts (they sum/count per category); pre-aggregate in SQL only if the detail table itself should show summary rows

composition.notes: grid columns are TWIPS summing to the printable width (portrait default: 12240 - 2*1440 = 9360). Landscape: page.widthTwips 15840 x heightTwips 12240 and rescale columns (e.g. 6480+6480 at margin 1440)

name: Pivot / matrix report (format-forked: SQL-pivoted flat table for RTF, native Crosstab for XPT)
description: A matrix ('column per month/SKU/status') delivered per format: RTF = a FLAT table over columns already pivoted in SQL (PIVOT / SUM(CASE)); XPT = the native interactive Crosstab aggregating long detail rows. The template never computes the pivot.
whenToUse: Any 'pivot / matrix / column per X' ask. Print -> RTF fork (recipe.blocks): pivot in SQL, template shows a flat table. Interactive -> XPT fork (recipe.xpt): native Crosstab is legitimate (22 real corpus files). NEVER build the pivot with per-cell template sums (lp:anti:template-wide-pivot).
intents: pivot by SKU with one column per month
matrix of quantity by region and period
crosstab of counts by status and day
column per quarter with a total column
spreadsheet style summary rows by regions columns by months

requires.dataShape: RTF fork: one wide row per line (REGION, JAN_QTY, FEB_QTY, ...) with the column set FIXED at design time. XPT fork: LONG detail rows (REGION, MONTH_NAME, QTY) - the Crosstab aggregates them
requires.preAggregation: RTF fork: PIVOT or SUM(CASE WHEN ...) columns in SQL, plus a SQL total column when wanted. XPT fork: none - the aggregation lives in the Crosstab

composition.notes: ONE row, TWO recipes (recipe.blocks = rtf, recipe.xpt = crosstab in a grid cell) so the existing lp:anti:template-wide-pivot redirect resolves for both formats. The RTF totals row sums each pivoted COLUMN once - one sum per column is fine; per-CELL cross-group sums are the banned per-cell construct

recipe.notes: RTF fork = blocks (flat table over SQL-pivoted columns); XPT fork = xpt (native Crosstab; crosstab components live in grid cells)

pitfalls: DYNAMIC column sets (columns discovered at runtime) are NOT supported - BIP's answer is horizontal-break-table, which our generator does not emit yet (lp:cap:horizontal-break-table); fix the column set in SQL at design time.
XPT Crosstab: filter with filters:[...], not an XPath predicate (lp:anti:xpath-predicate-on-xpt-datatable).
Never emulate the pivot with per-cell template sums (lp:anti:template-wide-pivot) - it renders but is unmaintainable and banned.

name: Chart block nested inside a forEach loop
description: Placing a {kind:'chart'} block among a forEach's child blocks to get 'a chart in each section'.
intents: a chart inside each customer section
repeat the pie chart per department
graph within the loop for every group
per section chart in the printed report
same chart appears many times down the page
trigger: a chart placed among forEach children, or the ask 'a chart for/under each X'
why: The chart shape is re-emitted on EVERY iteration - N copies march down the page (verified duplication), and since the chart's group.select is absolute every copy shows the SAME data. The builder's teaching error spells it out: charts must sit at TOP level.
alternative: Put ONE chart block at top level before the forEach (chart-on-first-page), or fixed per-category charts side-by-side via the grid (chart|chart). True per-group mini-charts are not supported by the generator.

name: Absolute path on an inner group under an outer forEach
description: Writing an inner forEach/table group (or the invoice shape's linesGroup) as an absolute /DATA_DS/... path while an outer group wraps it.
intents: inner loop bound to the full data path
lines group as an absolute path inside the master loop
every section repeats all rows of the whole report
totals show the grand total in every group
trigger: an inner forEach/table group (or linesGroup with outerGroup set) starting with '/'
why: Every outer iteration walks EVERY node in the document: each master repeats ALL rows of all masters, and absolute sum() totals aggregate across the whole document. buildInvoiceRtf rejects it loudly ('linesGroup ... is ABSOLUTE while outerGroup ... is set - use a path RELATIVE to the outer group'); in raw blocks[] it silently renders a plausible-looking WRONG report.
alternative: Only the OUTERMOST forEach is absolute (/DATA_DS/G_MASTER); every nested group and every totals sum() path is RELATIVE to its enclosing group (G_LINE, sum(G_LINE/AMOUNT)).

name: Wrong chart vocabulary for the format (XPT keys in an RTF chart, or the reverse)
description: Writing an RTF chart block with the XPT chart keys (type / dimensionField / string group / measures[].name / agg:'summation'), or an XPT chart with the RTF keys (graphType / group:{select,by} / measures[].field).
intents: rtf chart with dimensionField and type keys
chart renders a No data to display frame
reuse the xpt chart json inside the rtf template
builder rejected my chart keys
agg summation in an rtf chart measure
trigger: chart keys from the other format's dialect - the two dialects are NOT interchangeable
why: Wrong keys used to flow straight into the Graph XML as graphType="undefined" select="undefined" and render a silent 'No data to display' frame at HTTP 200. The RTF builder now auto-translates the unambiguous cases and REJECTS the rest with a per-key fix message (e.g. 'dimensionField is not a field - it belongs in group.by'; 'agg summation - you meant sum').
alternative: RTF dialect: graphType + group:{select,by} + measures:[{label,field,agg:sum|count|avg}]. XPT dialect: type + dimensionField + measures:[{name,agg:summation|count|average}] + seriesField. Read the builder's teaching error and swap keys - do not conclude the format 'cannot do charts'.

name: XPath predicate used to filter an XPT DataTable/Crosstab
description: Filtering an interactive DataTable or Crosstab by baking an XPath predicate into the group path (filter:'DAYS <= 1' or /G_ROW[DAYS<=1]/COL) instead of the real filters block.
intents: xpt detail table shows zero rows after adding a filter
last 24 hours condition on the data table
filter the interactive table with an xpath predicate
table went empty when I added a where condition
crosstab filtered by a predicate returns nothing
trigger: an .xpt table/crosstab spec using the XPath `filter` knob or a predicated field path
why: The interactive processor cannot derive the repeating context from a predicated path - the DataTable renders 0 ROWS (verified). XPath predicates remain valid for RTF for-each and for XPT CHART aggregation; DataTable/Crosstab need the native filters block. Related silent failure: a filter referencing an UNDECLARED field blanks the whole component - the builder auto-declares filter fields in the businessView to prevent this.
alternative: filters:[{field:'DAYS_AGO',operator:'less_or_equal',value:1}] emits the native <filters> block (what Oracle's own ESS dashboard uses). Operators: equal, not_equal, greater, less, greater_or_equal, less_or_equal, top_n, is_null, not_null.

name: Two or more measures on an interactive XPT chart
description: Binding 2+ measures[] to one .xpt chart (e.g. NUMBER_OF_SUCCEEDED and NUMBER_OF_ERROR as two series), usually because the data was pre-aggregated into wide columns.
intents: stacked bar with succeeded and error columns as two measures

XMLElement getChildNodes param is null
trigger: an .xpt ChartSpec with measures.length > 1, or wide pre-aggregated measure columns feeding a chart
why: A multi-measure XPT chart renders when it is ALONE on the page but FAULTS ('XMLElement.getChildNodes() param is null') the moment a second chart shares the page - the builder now rejects >1 measures with the fix in the error. Wide pre-aggregated columns are also the wrong data shape for an interactive chart.
alternative: ONE measure + a series DIMENSION: dimensionField:'RUN_DAY', seriesField:'STATUS', measures:[{name:'REQUEST_ID',agg:'count'}] - multi-series comes from seriesField, and the model feeds long/detail rows, not wide columns. (SCATTER's 2-measure X,Y form is the schema-documented exception.)

name: Grid units swapped between formats (twips vs pixels)
description: Copying grid column widths across formats: pixel values (560/1044) into an RTF grid, or twips values (4200/7800) into an XPT LayoutGrid.
intents: dashboard grid renders blank after setting column widths
column widths 4200 and 7800 in the xpt grid
grid columns squashed into a narrow sliver
reuse the rtf grid widths in the interactive layout
cells pushed off the page
trigger: grid column numbers that are plausible in the OTHER format's unit
why: The two grids use different units. XPT LayoutGrid columns are PIXELS (sum ~1554 for a 1650px page): twips-scale values push cells OFF-PAGE and the layout renders BLANK (verified). RTF grid columns are TWIPS (1440/inch, printable ~9360 on the portrait default): px-scale values collapse the grid into a ~1-inch sliver.
alternative: RTF: columns in twips summing to the printable width (pageWidth - 2*margin, default 9360). XPT: columns in px summing to ~pageWidth - 96 (1554 at the 1650px default). RTF column widths on TABLE columns are twips too.

name: Subtemplate import wrapped in a conditional
description: Putting a <?import:xdoxsl:///...xsb?> inside if/choose ('only import the chrome when X'), or trying to pick imports per condition.

trigger: an import that the user/agent wants gated by a condition
why: BIP resolves imports when the template opens: imports must be UNCONDITIONAL at the very top of the body, and an import inside a conditional (or one that cannot resolve) kills the WHOLE template - nothing renders. The builder's imports[] deliberately cannot express a conditional import; it always emits them unconditionally first.
alternative: Import ALWAYS; make the CALL conditional instead - callTemplate has a when:'cond' knob that wraps only the call (<?if:cond?><?call-template:N?><?end if?>), or use choose/when around alternative callTemplate blocks.
